title: Saving on House Construction Costs Without Cutting Quality: 7 Ways
desc: 7 ways to cut building costs while keeping quality: optimise design, fix drawings early, choose materials well, accept work by stage, never cut the wrong things.
summary: Sensible ways to reduce building costs from design and materials to construction management, and the items that should never be cut.
body: Saving when building does not mean choosing the cheapest workers or the worst materials. The most lasting savings come from sound design, a clear plan and little rework. Here are 7 ways you can apply.

A compact plan with few corners and little elaborate decoration, and sensible room sizes, reduces the volume of concrete, steel, formwork and labour. For a house that must be designed by a qualified person (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP), good design fees are usually repaid through less waste in construction.

Changing the design during construction is the biggest source of extra cost: demolition, redoing work, buying more materials. The unit price for additional quantities must be agreed before the work is done (Clause 3, Article 23 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP), which means every change of mind costs more. Take time to review the layout, plumbing, electrical and interior drawings carefully before signing the construction contract.
Structure: foundations, columns, beams and slabs must follow the design of a qualified person; saving here can be paid for with safety.
Waterproofing: bathroom floors, roof terrace, roof and adjoining walls – fixing leaks later costs many times more.
Concealed electrical and plumbing: low-quality wires and pipes are hard to replace once plastered and tiled.
Materials must be conformity-certified: some construction materials must have a certificate of conformity – see Construction materials that must be conformity-certified.
Grade by area: use better materials in the living room and facade; use moderate ones in storage, the drying yard and secondary rooms.
Write a ceiling unit price in the contract so you can choose freely and pay only the difference.
Prefer standard, widely available tile and door sizes to reduce cutting waste.
Compare at least 2–3 sellers, and get invoices and warranty slips.

The owner is responsible for organising construction, supervision and safety (Clause 3, Article 10). Checking the quality of materials before they are used and accepting each stage (foundations, reinforcement before pouring concrete, plumbing and electrical before plastering) helps detect errors early, when fixing them is still cheap. See Acceptance of residential buildings and Is it compulsory to hire a supervisor when building a house?.
6. Make proper use of exemptions and reductions

A self-built house of a household or individual is exempt from the registration fee when registering ownership (Clause 11, Article 10 of Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC). Building in accordance with the permit is also a saving: building contrary to the permit can be fined and ordered to be demolished – see How much is the fine for building without a permit or contrary to the permit?.

A house that is cheap to build but costly in electricity because it is hot, or costly to repair because of leaks and cracks, is not really cheap. Sensible ventilation and shading, durable materials and a periodic maintenance plan reduce costs for many years – see Maintenance of houses and buildings. Every building must be surveyed and designed by qualified professionals; do not change the structure or materials from the design on your own. The specific provisions of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP are compulsory only for state-funded and PPP projects.
